photos_ranked: Parker: Parker, from my World Inside Me series. I layered the portrait with branches and water.
Austen: My friend Austen, with driftwood layered into his portrait for World Inside Me.
City Hall After Dark: Philadelphia City Hall at night. I waited for the street to clear so the building could carry the whole frame.
Silverstone, in the rain: I took this at Silverstone during the British Grand Prix. The spray almost hides the car behind.
Watcher: A close-up portrait from my Superhero project, edited in Photoshop.
Light Trails: A long exposure over the expressway in Philadelphia. The red and white streams split the frame down the middle.
Vertical Spit: A drill and a rotisserie, paired for my Cause and Effect series.
Golden Lion Tamarin: A quieter subject from my animal photographs.
Ferrari at Silverstone: Another of my Silverstone photographs, with the Ferrari side-on.
Checkmate: My Digital Dali composite, with the chess pieces brought close to the camera.
Low Tide, Reassembled: A shoreline taken apart and put back together for my Fragmentation project.
Snooze: An alarm and spilled coffee, paired for Cause and Effect.
Throw-In: From my Back to School series. I kept the player in color against the field.
Cocktail Hour: Several versions of the same subject in my Multiplicity composite.
Bayside Sunset: Trees on the shore holding the last of the light, with the sky doing most of the work.
Loki: My cat. Here, his eyes catch the light before the rest of him does.
Through the spray: My view through the rain at Silverstone. The curbing leads back toward the car.
Measured Stride: A measurement at the desk, then a stride on the pitch. From Cause and Effect.
Rebound: Two moments from the same possession, side by side.
Calvert Street: A Baltimore corner, desaturated and then hand-colored so only what I chose keeps its color.
LOVE, moving: Trying something less still in my Philadelphia night series.
Ball in the air: A film frame with just enough sky to separate the ball from the player.
Skid: A skateboard wheel crashing through a wave of foam pellets.
Nine Lives: One cat, one room, many places at once.
A building doubled: Looking up at a building and its reflection. Part of my film work.
Orange Route: A city bus and steam in black and white, with the signs colored back in by hand.
Rocky shoreline: Getting close to the rocks for this shoreline frame.
Dominion curve: Dominion, from my side of the track. I liked the curve against the autumn trees.
Pour: A coffee shot from above, split down the middle between cream and black.
Across the basin: A wider view from the same cherry-blossom series.
Sun over the water: I let the water take most of this vertical frame.
Last strip of sun: A thin strip of orange over the water.
Car meet: From my car-meet photos. Two red cars, with one tucked behind the other.
Blossoms: From my cherry-blossom photos. I kept the nearest flowers sharp and let the branches soften.
Blossoms and stone: From my cherry-blossom photos in Washington.
Passing in both directions: Another long exposure from my Philadelphia night series.
Windows at night: A tighter frame from the same evening in Philadelphia.
At the water’s edge: A low view from my landscape photos, following the rocks into the water.
Blue BMW: Another frame from my car-meet photos. The blue paint and white wheels stood out.
Under the blossoms: A little more room for people in this frame.
Into the bend: Another frame from my day at Dominion, following the car into the bend.
The pitch at sunset: Soccer is a big part of my life. This frame is about the field around the game.
Street after dark: I like photographing streets at night. Here, the lamps and road markings do most of the work.
Down the street: Philadelphia after dark, with the street nearly empty.
Steam against brick: From my film work. Soft steam against a very rigid wall.
Stone and leaves: Looking up, on film. I like the leaves breaking up all those straight lines.
Branches in layers: One of my closer film studies, with branches crossing in and out of focus.
Winter lamp: A winter detail on film. The snow picks out the top of the lamp.
Snow and timber: A winter detail from my film prints: timber, snow, and the woods behind.
By the car: Cars in my film work, too. I kept the person just beyond the hood.
Empty chairs: A quieter frame from my film work: two chairs and a fire ring.
Glass and gesture: A closer film frame, with the hand and reflections overlapping.
On the grass: One of my film prints. I kept the frame close to the small gesture at the knee.
Before the kick: From my soccer photos: the pause before the kick.
Resistance training: Training, from my soccer album. A different part of the sport than match day.
Down the hall: A low viewpoint from my Philadelphia series.
Food cart, New York: A wide-angle frame from my New York photos. I kept the circular lens edge.
Pedicabs, New York: Pedicabs and signs from my New York photos. I kept the purple barrier in front.
New York sidewalk: From my New York series. I let the wide-angle lens pull the buildings inward.
At the crosswalk: Down near street level for this New York frame.
Branches overhead: Looking up instead of across the water.
Evening sky: From my landscape photos. The cloud texture was what I wanted to keep.
Wheel detail: Getting closer at the car meet: spokes, bolts, and the brake behind them.
Under the bridge: One of the less obvious details from my landscape album.
Lines and texture: From my film prints. Overlapping textures around a utility pole and wires.
Gorilla and Infant: A mother and baby at the zoo, finished with a designed border.
Flight Paths: A classroom globe with flight routes drawn across it.
Red Fox: A fox nosing through the undergrowth.
Brady Bunch: Nine frames that pass objects from one box to the next.
Self-Portrait Collage: Me, built out of the pieces of my own photos.
Pull Station: A school fire alarm repeated in a grid, after Warhol.
